title: Symmetry-Preserving Variational Quantum Simulation of the Heisenberg Spin Chain on Noisy Quantum Hardware
summary: Demonstrates symmetry-preserving VQE on actual NISQ hardware for the Heisenberg spin chain. Key insight: deviation from exact results arises from controlled symmetry constraints rather than optimization failure. Validates that symmetry-preserving gate sets are practically viable on hardware.
key_findings: Symmetry-constrained VQE circuits achieve correct ground states on noisy hardware
Deviation from exact results quantified as a function of symmetry constraint strength
Error arises from symmetry constraints, not optimizer failure — confirms our SIM-2026-008 diagnosis
Applicable to spin-1/2 chains with Z2 or other discrete symmetries
project_relevance: Directly validates our SIM-2026-008 hypothesis that parity-preserving gate sets are viable. Confirms that the ~3.33% energy floor in SIM-2026-008c is a structural consequence of symmetry enforcement, not optimizer failure — exactly what we found. The paper's framework for quantifying symmetry-constraint-induced error gap could help us predict what energy floor to expect at 24q.
